name: Tamar (Absalom's sister, David's daughter)
title: David's Daughter Who Was Violated
summary: Tamar was a daughter of King David and the sister of Absalom. She was raped by her half-brother Amnon, an event that led to deep family conflict and eventually Absalom's revenge and rebellion against his father David. Her tragic fate illustrates the destructive consequences of sin within David's royal household.

keyEvents.title: Amnon's Desire for Tamar
keyEvents.description: Amnon, David's firstborn son, fell ill with desire for his half-sister Tamar. His cousin Jonadab devised a cunning plan so that Amnon could have Tamar alone.

keyEvents.title: Tamar's Rape
keyEvents.description: Amnon tricked Tamar into coming to his bedroom by pretending he was sick and asking her to prepare food for him. Despite Tamar's pleas and protests, Amnon overpowered her and raped her.

keyEvents.title: Amnon Rejects Tamar
keyEvents.description: After the assault, Amnon's desire turned to hatred, and he drove Tamar away. Tamar tore her special long-sleeved robe and put ashes on her head as a sign of grief and shame.

keyEvents.title: Absalom Takes Tamar In
keyEvents.description: Absalom understood what had happened when he saw his sister in mourning. He took her into his house, and Tamar lived there as a lonely woman. Absalom hated Amnon for what he had done.

keyEvents.title: Absalom's Revenge on Amnon
keyEvents.description: After two years, Absalom planned his revenge. During a sheep shearing, he invited all the king's sons and ordered his servants to kill Amnon when he was drunk. The murder was directly motivated by the assault on Tamar.

keyEvents.title: David's Passivity
keyEvents.description: King David was furious when he heard about the assault on Tamar, but he did nothing to punish Amnon. David's inaction contributed to the escalating conflict within the royal family that eventually led to Absalom's rebellion.
